original_question: Does there exist a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem? Here K_2 is the class of groups of 2-knots, so the question asks whether some group of a 2-knot has no algorithm deciding, for an arbitrary word in its generators, whether that word represents the identity element.
target_in_paper: Section 7, concluding questions, question (1): "Is there a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem ? Conjecture: Yes."
correct_elements: The draft matches the paper's actual open problem essentially verbatim. It correctly identifies K_2 as the class of 2-knot groups and correctly interprets "unsolvable word problem" as the nonexistence of an algorithm deciding whether an arbitrary word represents the identity.
missing_details: In the paper, a 2-knot is specifically a locally flat PL embedding of S^2 in S^4; the authors state that throughout Section 2 they work in the PL category and all embeddings are locally flat.
A 2-knot group means the fundamental group of the complement of such an embedding, i.e. a group of the form pi_1(S^4 - K) for a locally flat PL 2-knot K.
The paper presents this as an open question and explicitly conjectures that the answer is yes.
The existential quantifier is over members of K_2 itself; this should not be broadened to the separate neighboring question of whether every finitely presented group embeds in a 2-knot group.
Since groups in K_2 are finitely presented (cf. the presentation characterization in Theorem 2.5), the word problem should be understood in the usual finite-presentation sense.
refined_question: Does there exist a locally flat PL 2-knot K subset S^4 such that its complement group G = pi_1(S^4 - K), equivalently a group G in K_2, has unsolvable word problem?
justification: This is the paper's exact concluding open problem, stated as question (1) in Section 7. The introduction flags the same issue as the unknown hypothesis needed to settle the remaining K_2 case of the paper's recognition results, and it explicitly says the authors do not know whether 2-knot groups with unsolvable word problem exist. Section 2 provides the needed scope: the paper works with locally flat PL embeddings, defines an n-knot as an embedded S^n in S^{n+2}, and defines K_n to be the class of groups of n-knots, so for n = 2 the relevant objects are groups pi_1(S^4 - K) of locally flat PL 2-knots K. I did not replace the draft by the broader adjacent question about embedding all finitely presented groups in 2-knot groups, because the paper lists that separately as question (2).
